elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to an Affiliate.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits either Party, including PB as Customer, to assign the Agreement and all rights and obligations to any Affiliate without the other Party's consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a merger.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits assignment to a successor in connection with a transfer of the relevant business or assets and expressly includes a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits assignment to a successor in connection with a sale or other transfer and expressly includes sale of stock, sale of assets, or otherwise, which covers an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 expressly permits assignment to a successor in connection with a transfer of all or substantially all of the business or assets to which the Agreement relates.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's prior consent.
elements.evidence: Although Section 15.6 begins with a mutual-consent rule, it permits SFJ as Vendor to assign without PB's consent to any Affiliate or qualifying successor.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no reasonableness limitation on PB's exercise of any consent right.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor under any circumstances.
elements.evidence: There is no competitor prohibition. The Affiliate and successor exceptions could permit an assignment to a PB competitor without PB's consent.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement because of a Customer Change of Control.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.6 expressly states that a Change of Control of PB shall not give SFJ any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 permits PB to assign the entire Agreement without consent to a qualifying successor.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 mutually permits SFJ to assign the entire Agreement without consent to a qualifying successor.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning the Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 imposes no written-notice requirement for successor assignments. Section 14.2.6 only requires PB to notify SFJ regarding a definitive Change of Control agreement and does not cover every successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning the Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: No provision requires SFJ to give written notice of a successor assignment.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to successors require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 allows PB to assign to an Affiliate without consent, even where the Affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Section 15.6 allows SFJ to assign to an Affiliate without consent, even where the Affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to other Customer assignments.
elements.evidence: The general prior-written-consent requirement contains no obligation for SFJ to act reasonably.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to other Vendor assignments.
elements.evidence: The general prior-written-consent requirement contains no obligation for PB to act reasonably.

result.reason: Assuming PB is Customer and SFJ is Vendor, the redline successfully removes SFJ's Change-of-Control termination right and preserves PB's Affiliate and successor assignment rights. It does not impose the preferred Vendor-side consent and competitor restrictions, and it does not satisfy the fallback because successor notice and reasonableness duties are absent while Affiliate assignments remain exempt from consent. It is not minimal because it reaches neither complete position and broadly prohibits any Change-of-Control-related acceleration, increase, or modification of PB payment obligations, potentially affecting provisions beyond the targeted termination remedy. Section 15.6 also ends with a dangling “and,” and the phrase “where applicable guarantee” is uncertain, materially reducing drafting quality.
